title: the inspector's own-dialog excuse reads the journal as an index
intention: _only_own_dialog excuses the journal when every line it gained or lost since HEAD names the crossing ticket's own log, because a door write now replaces that path's one index line instead of appending.
traces_to: Law 3: working_tree_clean would report a refused crossing's own record as dirt, a red it did not measure. Law 9: 3ba20f30a585's excuse would be quietly dead.
how: For the journal path, take set(HEAD lines) ^ set(working lines). The difference is non-empty and every line in it parses and names tid's log. The log path keeps its byte-prefix rule. It builds after b15da5656579 lands, which adds read_trail and the index.

clauses.claim: over a committed scratch index, tid's gate dialog written through the door is excused
an index line for any other path, changed or added, is still dirt

why: Split from b15da5656579 under RULE 1. Akien, 16:47 UTC 2026-11-16, relayed verbatim by the orchestrator: "then how about this... the latest entry remains in cairn commons, and everything else broken into... per day? per week? inside of our .cairn/logs folder". After b15d the journal holds only the newest entry per path and every entry is in a day trail on this box for 30 days.

decisions.text: D1: the reader reads as the intention says.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

out: every other component; cairn/tools/artifact is b15da5656579's
